gap: Measured (not modeled) household waste for most countries
why_it_matters: Estimates for countries without studies are extrapolated, so models learn from guesses.
how_to_close: Standardized household waste audits; smart-bin data

gap: Store-level surplus data
why_it_matters: Retail surplus is private, so matching it to food banks can't be trained or evaluated.
how_to_close: Partnerships with grocers; anonymized POS + markdown data

gap: Street-level outcomes (heat illness, flooded addresses)
why_it_matters: Reanalysis is about 30 km resolution; harm is measured at the block.
how_to_close: Hospital heat-illness records; insurance and 311 flood reports

gap: Continuous homelessness data
why_it_matters: Point-in-Time counts are a single night a year and undercount hidden homelessness.
how_to_close: Linked shelter, school and health records with consent

gap: Eviction filings
why_it_matters: Not in either dataset, but the most direct leading signal.
how_to_close: Court records (e.g. Eviction Lab)

gap: Open bulk living-wage data
why_it_matters: MIT's data requires a license beyond 10 locations, so a free tool can't redistribute it.
how_to_close: License request; or build an open cost-of-living estimate

gap: Wages by employer
why_it_matters: Public wage data is by sector and region, not by employer.
how_to_close: Job-posting pay ranges (pay transparency laws)

gap: How young people actually use AI companions
why_it_matters: Usage data sits with companies; surveys rely on self-report.
how_to_close: Privacy-preserving data donation by teens and families; researcher access to platform data

gap: Outcomes of youth programs
why_it_matters: Most youth-connection nonprofits don't publish measured outcomes, so effects can't be compared.
how_to_close: Shared outcome measures across grantees (loneliness and belonging scales)

gap: Frontier model internals
why_it_matters: Interpretability work mostly runs on small open models; frontier weights and training data are closed.
how_to_close: Researcher access programs; open-weight frontier releases

gap: Energy per answer: local vs. data center
why_it_matters: No good open comparison of how much energy a query costs on a laptop vs. in a data center, so the case for local AI is unproven.
how_to_close: Measure it: open benchmarks of energy per token across hardware

gap: Individual-level consumption and screen-time data
why_it_matters: Purchase and usage data sits with retailers and platforms, not researchers.
how_to_close: Data donation by consenting users; platform transparency rules

gap: How many academic child-safety tools reach real use
why_it_matters: No source gives a count or rate, so nobody can say how much published research is ever deployed.
how_to_close: Track each published tool: what was released, who runs it, and when support ended

gap: Whether an open AI tool is actually used
why_it_matters: No tracker checked records deployment as a field, and downloads and stars are weak stand-ins for real use.
how_to_close: Record documented deployments with a source and a date, next to the raw download and commit signals

gap: Survival of AI-for-good fellowship and civic-tech projects
why_it_matters: No audit was found of how many of these projects are still running, so the often-quoted failure rates have no solid source.
how_to_close: Check each program's public repositories for last commit, archived status and a named user

gap: Share of Hugging Face models with zero downloads after 2023
why_it_matters: The last measured figure (71%) is from October 2023, before the Hub grew past 2 million models.
how_to_close: Recompute it from the daily Hub snapshot

gap: Regular data for every goal indicator
why_it_matters: About 70% of the 234 indicators have good country coverage; one 2025 review counts 66 that are not regularly produced.
how_to_close: Fund national statistics offices; the UN's 2025 report calls data the essential infrastructure for the goals

gap: Direct food security surveys in every country at risk
why_it_matters: Where surveys are missing, the World Food Programme has to estimate hunger with models instead of measuring it.
how_to_close: More frequent phone and household surveys

gap: A registry of households and their incomes
why_it_matters: Togo had none, so phone-based targeting was the best option available, and it still left out people without phones.
how_to_close: Build social registries; combine them with phone and satellite data

gap: Gender-equality goal data in most countries
why_it_matters: UN Women's 2025 report implies only about 61% of this data is available globally, against 84% in the eight countries its programme supports.
how_to_close: Extend support for national statistics offices to more countries
